implementation_notes: The maintained MPMC channel used in production: bounded/unbounded, select! for multiplexing, send_timeout/recv_timeout for deadlines, and select_biased for a priority order. This is the right default over std::sync::mpsc when more than one consumer is needed or when select is required.
code_sketch: select! { recv(rx) -> m => handle(m?), send(tx, job) -> _ => {}, default(d) => {} }
pitfalls: select! picks randomly; use select_biased! for priority.
A closed channel yields Err on recv - handle it as termination.

variants.name: std::sync::mpsc (MSPC, closes on sender drop)
variants.implementation_notes: The standard synchronous channel. Its cleanest feature is the close: when the last Sender drops, the receiver's loop ends with no sentinel and no close call - termination is tied to ownership. sync_channel(n) bounds it and blocks the sender when full (backpressure).
pitfalls: Cloning a Sender somewhere long-lived prevents the close.
